queue.title: Data releases in the US yesterday were a mixed bag, offering some support to the dollar but failing to solve the market's conundrum about the September FOMC (pricing now 9bp). Core PCE, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, printed in line with expectations at 0.2% month-on-month and 3.3% year-on-year, suggesting disinflation remains on track but at a frustratingly gradual pace. Headline PCE came in slightly firmer at 0.2% MoM and 3.7% YoY, prompting a small hawkish repricing in the USD curve.
queue.resumo: The growth side of the report was softer. Real personal spending was unchanged in July despite higher real disposable income, with households opting to save rather than spend. Real household disposable income has effectively flatlined for more than a year. Overall, we remain reasonably confident in our call for the Fed to hold on 16 September and, by extension, in a weaker dollar. That said, the next three weeks may need to bring a more convincing combination of data and Fedspeak before markets move closer to a hold outcome. queue.title: Tokyo CPI for August is released at 00:30 BST tomorrow. The headline is expected to inch lower to 1.9% (from 2% in July) and core to 1.8% (from 1.9%). A close-to-consensus print should not derail market confidence on a rate hike by the Bank of Japan on 18 September (21bp currently in the price), after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called for a policy follow-up to FX intervention and July CPI surprised on the upside.
queue.resumo: The two-year USDJPY swap rate differential has shrunk by around 35bp in the past 30 days, but the yen has failed to attract buyers below 158. With a lot of BoJ tightening in the price, the risks are that officials disappoint markets on the dovish side even if they hike in September. Ultimately, a dovish Fed repricing remains the most tangible path to keep USD/JPY below 160.

queue.title: As bolsas asiáticas fecharam mistas, após perspectiva da Nvidia renovar a confiança no setor de IA. Os ganhos permaneceram desiguais, já que os investidores avaliaram os custos mais altos de memória, inflação persistente e expectativa de alta nos juros. O desempenho irregular reflete preocupações como a falta de receita de data centers chineses na última previsão da Nvidia, que alertou para a escassez de memória e o aumento dos custos de componentes. Os mercados de títulos continuam limitando a valorização das techs. O vice do BoJ, Ryozo Himino, afirmou que o aumento oportuno dos juros poderia ajudar a evitar que a inflação forçasse aumentos abruptos mais tarde, mantendo aberta a possibilidade de outra alta já em setembro. Kospi subiu 1,53% mesmo após o BC aumentar juros em 25 pb, a 3%, por crescimento acima do esperado, inflação acima da meta e os riscos à estabilidade financeira. Xangai +1,13%; Shenzhen +1,50%; Nikkei caiu -0,20% e o Hang Seng recuou -0,34%%; Taiex +0,31%.

queue.title: As bolsas europeias operam sem direção única nesta 5ªF, com a tendência negativa predominando, com a queda dos setores de bens de consumo, produtos químicos e automotivos anulando a força do segmento de tecnologia, impulsionado pelo balanço melhor do que o esperado da Nvidia. Nesse cenário, as principais ações francesas se destacam entre as maiores baixas diante de resultados trimestrais considerados decepcionantes. A fabricante de bebidas Pernod Ricard, por exemplo, recuava 7,04% após divulgar queda nas vendas líquidas anuais. Já entre as techs, a ASML Holding ganhava 1,44%, a Infineon Technologies avançava 4,15% e a STMicroelectronics tinha alta de 4,43%. Há pouco, a bolsa de Londres cedia 0,48%; a de Frankfurt subia 0,25% e a de Paris perdia 1,18%. Os índices STOXX 50 (-0,21%) e STOXX 600 (-0,34%) registravam baixa.
